briefing_title_en: Daily Briefing, Oct 12, 2026: AI Guardrails and Self-Improving Agents, Riyadh Airport Strikes, EU Caps Chinese Hybrid EV Imports
briefing_summary_en: The October 12 briefing spans AI, developer, science, startup, world, China, finance and opinion sections. AI coverage includes arXiv papers on falsifiable world models, byte-level multimodal foundation models, speculative decoding and runtime agent guardrails, while Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella says models need an 'emergency brake.' In developer news, Python 3.15.0 enters GitHub Actions and Dwarf Fortress adopts version control. Abroad, a second Houthi strike on Riyadh airport killed one and injured 11, Panama declared an emergency after earthquakes, and the EU confirmed a 350,000-a-year cap on Chinese hybrid EV imports. Finance tracks earnings, oil swings, a higher-rate outlook and the RBI's rupee defense at 97. Opinion coverage includes Linux phones, browser fingerprinting, passkeys and differences in shared understanding of LLM capabilities.

sections.briefing_title_en: AI and Large Models: Falsifiable World Models, Elastic Recurrence, and Agent Guardrails
sections.briefing_summary_en: This briefing covers final articles in AI and large models across frontier models and research and governance.
